boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Round Mountain record (November 19, 1861) in Operations in the Indian Territory [November-December 1861]. Cooper's march from the Deep Fork and his return to Concharta are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, reinforcements and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field names the Creeks and Seminoles and the Indian Department without figures; the live field is blank. The frozen description says Cooper set out with about 1,400; Cooper says about 1,400 moved up the Deep Fork and that Opothleyahola's force was variously estimated at 800 to 1,200 Creeks and Seminoles and 200 to 300 negroes. Britton gives Cooper fourteen hundred and says the chief estimated he could bring about fifteen hundred into the field.
claims.rationale: Column and estimated opposing figures; no return. No account by Opothleyahola's side was inspected; every figure for his force and losses is an opponent's estimate or a history's. None is adopted as a matched opening strength.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory; the frozen description says the Confederates claimed victory because the chief left the area. Cooper says the enemy made good his retreat under cover of darkness; Britton says the Union Indians drove the first attackers from the field before retreating north in the night.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads Unknown; the live field reads 10 (US 0; CS 10). Cooper gives his entire loss as 1 captain and 5 men killed and further wounded and missing in a garbled line, and prisoners' estimate of the enemy's loss as a figure read '1 10' in OCR. Britton says the attackers lost upward of twenty killed and wounded in the first repulse.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Cooper's garbled wounded figures are not decoded.

open_questions: The live NPS page has an empty description; the frozen CWSAC description is that family's narrative. Brinson's No. 2 and Young's No. 3 reports on Round Mountain, returns and maps remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live battle page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Cooper's January 20, 1862 report covers all three engagements and is an interested Confederate account; it is written after McIntosh's January 1 report and criticizes McIntosh. Wiley Britton's The Civil War on the Border, vol. I (second edition, 1891) is a retrospective history by a Union soldier of the border army, based by its title page on the official reports; it is not independent of the report families. Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
